data.narrative:
Nord Quantique, a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Julien Camirand Lemyre and Philippe St-Jean, has raised C$40M+ including a C$23M tranche from Quantum Champions in December 2025. The quantum computing sector contains a comp universe of 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation method given data constraints. Using the C$40M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage transitions, the analysis implies a C$100M post-money valuation. Peer-median comparison was not viable; while 8 quantum computing comparables exist, insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints (fewer than 3 in any filtered cohort) precluded reliable benchmarking without introducing sector-wide noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of C$85M–C$115M, with C$100M as the median point. This range reflects application of a single method and carries material uncertainty around appropriate stage-progression multiples for quantum hardware at the current funding environment. Key risks to valuation include technology demonstration progress, competitive positioning within a crowded private comp set, and follow-on funding availability in a capital-constrained deep-tech sector.
